setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Werewolves Of London** (1 review): Warren Zevon song was a hit on FM radio in 1978 [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Happy Birthday Steve Parish**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **Phil's broken string & Happy Birthdays**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **Werewolves Of London**: rare: 12 archived performances [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-05-17.163478.aud.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 171 min [1]
- **gd78-05-17.akg.weiner.8334.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 172 min; rated 3.83/5 by 12 [3]. Said about its sound: Tape warbled during the song but resumed fine later; Intense bass drum punctuates transition into a cool Keith solo [9][10]
- **gd1978-05-17.sbd.scotton.miller.109000.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 165 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [5]. Said about its sound: Excellent transition from Lazy Lightning into Supplication [20]
- **gd1978-05-17.128393.naks.mason.partial.flac16**: source not stated; 11 songs; 95 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [7]

## Around the show

- Jerry did guitar work for Warren Zevon on that song [14]
- Reviewer was hooked by the time the band started this song [18]
- May 11, 1978 has a better version of this song [13]
- Seventh of twelve times played, all but three in 1978 [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-05-17.163478.aud.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Tim McKenzie; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes (unknown mics/deck) > Tim McKenzie's 2nd generation cassettes [1]. Also: Noah Weiner provided AKG D202E source for the beginning of the song [1]
- **gd78-05-17.akg.weiner.8334.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Noah Weiner; source: AKG D202E mics > Sony TC-152 [3]
- **gd1978-05-17.sbd.scotton.miller.109000.flac16**: taped by Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat -> CD [5]
- **gd1978-05-17.128393.naks.mason.partial.flac16**: taped by Mason B. Taylor; source: Both Sets Partial; Recorded By Mason Taylor on a Nakamichi 550 Cassette Deck, on chrome tapes, with Nakamichi microphones [7]. Also: Mason B. Taylor used Nakamichi 550 with shotgun mics for earlier recordings [7]
